evals.name: add-jsdoc-to-undocumented-utils
evals.prompt: Can you add proper JSDoc to the functions in dateUtils.ts? None of them are documented.
evals.expected_output: Every exported function gets a JSDoc block with a verb-led summary, @param for each parameter and @returns for the return value. Descriptions are terse and do NOT include {type} annotations (it's TypeScript). No code/behaviour changes. Surrounding formatting (no semicolons, single quotes) preserved.

evals.name: trim-noisy-comments
evals.prompt: This rateLimiter.ts file has way too many useless comments. Clean them up and make the whole thing less verbose.
evals.expected_output: Redundant comments that restate the code (e.g. '// set the max tokens', '// increment the token count', '// the constructor') are deleted. The genuine 'why' comment explaining the Math.min cap is kept (possibly shortened). The class and public methods gain a CRISP one-line summary — but NOT full @param/@returns tag blocks (this is a declutter pass, not a documenting pass; adding tags just trades one kind of verbosity for another). Net result is shorter and cleaner. No behaviour change.

evals.name: document-vue-script
evals.prompt: Do a documentation pass on the script in this SearchInput.vue component.
evals.expected_output: Functions (onInput, clear), the debounced runSearch, the computed and the watch get terse JSDoc/explanatory comments where useful. Noise comments inside functions ('// get the value from the input') are removed. The obvious per-prop noise comments are trimmed; defineProps/defineEmits are otherwise left alone. Template and styling are untouched.

evals.name: leave-well-documented-alone
evals.prompt: Give money.ts a documentation pass — make sure the functions are properly documented.
evals.expected_output: The file is already well-documented with terse JSDoc, full tags, no redundant types, and genuine 'why' comments. The skill should recognise this and make minimal-to-no changes — NOT rewrite, expand, or churn the existing good docs. Ideally it reports the file already meets the bar. Any edits should be tiny and justified (e.g. a genuinely missing tag), not stylistic churn.

evals.name: keep-business-rule-comments
evals.prompt: billing.ts is too verbose — trim the noisy comments.
evals.expected_output: Pure restatement comments ('// multiply the subtotal by the rate', '// add the tax...', '// start with the default', '// set days to 3 for the US') are deleted. The two comments that LOOK like restatement but actually encode external rules — the tax-authority round-half-up rationale and the AU/NPP next-business-day rule — are PRESERVED (the whole point: don't delete a 'why' just because it sits next to the line it explains). Functions gain a crisp one-line summary, NOT full @param/@returns tag blocks (declutter pass, not documenting pass). No logic change.

evals.name: js-file-needs-types-in-jsdoc
evals.prompt: Add JSDoc to the functions in stringUtils.js.
evals.expected_output: This is a plain .js file with no TypeScript types, so the JSDoc @param/@returns tags SHOULD include {type} annotations (e.g. @param {string} str, @returns {string}) — that's the only place the types are captured. All three functions documented with terse verb-led summaries. The optional `suffix` param noted as optional with its default.

evals.name: scope-to-mentioned-functions
evals.prompt: I just added parseConfig and validateConfig to configLoader.ts — can you make sure they're documented?
evals.expected_output: Only parseConfig and validateConfig get JSDoc (those are what the change introduced). The four pre-existing undocumented functions (readFile, mergeDefaults, deepClone, normalizeKeys) are LEFT ALONE — not swept into the doc pass — ideally with a one-line offer to document the rest if wanted. No logic change.

evals.name: capture-throws-and-units
evals.prompt: Document the withRetry function in retry.ts.
evals.expected_output: JSDoc whose summary conveys the non-obvious behaviour the signature hides — that it retries with EXPONENTIAL backoff. @param delayMs notes the unit (milliseconds) and that it's the base that doubles each attempt. @param attempts notes the >= 1 requirement. @throws documents both the RangeError when attempts < 1 AND that it rethrows the last error after exhausting attempts. @returns and @param fn documented. No redundant {type} (it's TS).
